outcome: Pregnancy success rate (defined as alive-birth and survival after neonatal period)
cohort: The study included 103 women with a history of recurrent pregnancy loss and 204 pregnant women receiving low-risk prenatal care, all seen at a university teaching hospital.
finding: Women with a history of recurrent pregnancy loss achieved a good reproductive success rate (91.2% of those who conceived), but experienced fewer full-term pregnancies, shorter pregnancy durations, and a higher rate of cesarean delivery compared to a low-risk control group.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery predominated in the recurrent pregnancy loss group (64.7%) compared to the control group (39.5%), predominantly due to gestational complications.
gest_age: Mean pregnancy duration was 34.8 weeks (SD=5.6) in the loss group versus 39.3 weeks (SD=1.6) in the control group; full-term pregnancies were also assessed.
